notes: Round 2. Chosen hook: 'TSMC PUTS UP TO / $1B IN AI LABS'. Clear in under 2 seconds: 8/10 (short, a name and a number; 'puts up to' is slightly clunky). Curiosity: 6/10 (who are the labs? why now?; 'AI LABS' is generic, but the tag line and slide 1 name OpenAI and Anthropic). Concrete number/name: 9/10 ($1B and TSMC). Promise kept: 9/10 (slide 1 says up to $1B in OpenAI and Anthropic; slide 2 splits it as up to $500M each on Nov. 10; the added 'up to' fixes the earlier overstatement and matches the facts). Reader stake: 2/10 (it is about a chipmaker and two labs, not the reader), which is acceptable because the other criteria are strong and nothing is overpromised. Compared with the others: option 1 (index 1, 'UP TO $1B FROM TSMC FOR AI LABS') is nearly equal but reads less cleanly. Option 2 (index 2, 'AI LABS GO FOR THEIR OWN CHIPS') has no number or name and hides the investment, which is the main news. Option 3 (index 3, 'UP TO $500M EACH FOR TWO AI LABS') leaves out TSMC, so the reader doesn't know who is paying. Chosen is the best. hook_types: all four labels are honest (number, number, claim, number); none is reader-impact. hook_pick_reason has a proper 'No reader-impact hook:' sentence that honestly says the articles state no direct effect on ordinary readers. Notes: (a) slides were not rendered locally, so the check used cover fields and slide text only, and the headline fit at render time is unchecked; (b) check at render that the tag line and slide 1 visibly name OpenAI and Anthropic, since the cover's 'AI LABS' relies on that.
